# Zero faces: lattice projection and a continuous-rank drop

This is a geometric/arithmetic consequence of reciprocal integrability at the current canonical positive-fiber limit. Together with exposed-face localization, it places the directional inverse-rate payment on finitely many exact face restrictions whose continuous affine rank is at most `d-2`. The restricted measures remain the actual defect measures; they are not automatically intrinsic uniform volume. Thus the result does not license applying OC to them as though they were ordinary convex-body mixed volume.

## 1. Canonical setting and the zero projection

Let `P` be a finite lattice-complete base, meaning

    P=conv(P) intersect Z^n.

Let `K_z` be positive `d`-dimensional compact convex fibers compatible under integer-base convex combinations, and let

    C=conv(union_{z in P} {z} x K_z).

Its sampled fibers are exactly the `K_z`. Let `L=min_i A_i` be nonnegative on `C`, positive on each sampled fiber interior, and suppose

    sum_{z in P} int_(K_z) 1/L(z,X) dX < infinity.

Fix one affine majorant `A>=L`, and suppose its exposed face

    F=C intersect {A=0}

is nonempty. Put `B=projection_z(F)` and `k=dim B`. Define

    Z_F={z in P: F_z is nonempty}.

Then exactly

    F=conv(union_{z in Z_F} {z} x F_z),
    B=conv Z_F,
    Z_F=B intersect Z^n.                             (1)

Indeed every point of the canonical hull is a convex combination of sampled-fiber points. Since `A>=0`, a combination has value zero only when all its positive-weight summands have value zero. This proves the first two equalities. Conversely, if an integer point lies in `B`, its fiber in `F` is nonempty by the definition of projection; lattice completeness places its base in `P`. This proves the last equality. In particular `B` is a lattice polytope, not an arbitrary convex projection with unrelated integer support.

The continuous gradient of `A` is nonzero. Otherwise `A` is constant on each fiber, and a nonempty zero fiber contradicts positivity of `L` in that fiber interior.

## 2. Reciprocal integrability excludes a zero facet in every sampled fiber

For `d>=2`, every nonempty `F_z` satisfies

    dim F_z <= d-2.                                (2)

It cannot have dimension `d` because `L` is positive in the interior. If it had dimension `d-1`, choose a compact relative `(d-1)`-ball `D` within that zero face, and choose `o` in `int K_z`. The cone `conv(D,o)` lies in `K_z`. For `0<s<A(z,o)/2`, its section at `A=s` is a homothetic copy of `D` with factor `1-s/A(z,o)>=1/2`. Coarea therefore gives

    int_(K_z) 1/A >= c int_0^(A(z,o)/2) ds/s = infinity.

Since `0<L<=A` in the interior, this contradicts integrability of `1/L`. This proves (2), with no smoothness or polyhedral assumption on the fibers.

For `d=1`, the same endpoint cone argument excludes any nonempty zero fiber. Hence under the reciprocal-mass hypotheses there is no such nonempty canonical `F`. The `d=0` parameter setting with positive sampled values likewise has no zero face.

## 3. The exact dimension formula over a relative-interior base

For any nonempty convex set `D` and its linear projection `E`, if `z` belongs to `relint E`, then

    dim D_z = dim D - dim E.                        (3)

Here the sets used are compact, so fibers are nonempty. A direct proof avoids a generic-position assertion. Choose `w_0` in `relint D`; a relative ball about it projects to a relative neighborhood of `z_0=projection(w_0)`, so `z_0 in relint E`. For any other `z in relint E`, extend the ray from `z_0` through `z` slightly inside `E` to write `z=(1-t)z_0+t z_1`, with `t<1` and `z_1 in E`. Lift `z_1` to `w_1 in D`. The point `(1-t)w_0+t w_1` lies in `relint D`, because it contains the corresponding scaled relative ball, and projects to `z`. Thus the fiber meets `relint D`. Its intersection with the affine hull has the kernel dimension `dim D-dim E`, and a relative ball in that kernel lies in the fiber. This proves (3).

Apply this to `F`, or to its restrictions over faces of `B`. Since `F` lies in the zero plane of an affine function with nonzero continuous gradient, its vertical affine kernel has dimension at most `d-1`. In particular

    dim F-dim B <= d-1.                             (4)

If equality holds in (4), the relative interior of `B` contains no integer point: such a point would have a zero fiber of dimension `d-1` by (3), contradicting (2).

Let `r=dim conv P`; the canonical body has dimension `r+d`. If `F` is a facet relative to that affine hull, then `dim F=r+d-1`. Inequality (4) forces `dim B=r`, and equality in (4) follows. Therefore every such zero facet has full relative base projection and lattice-free relative projected interior.

## 4. At most 2^k maximal sampled base faces

For each `z in B intersect Z^n`, let `E(z)` be its minimal face in the lattice polytope `B`. Let `E_1,...,E_h` be the distinct inclusion-maximal members of this finite family. They have the following properties:

* Every sampled base of `F` lies in at least one `E_l`.
* Each `E_l` has an integer point in its relative interior.
* The occupied parity classes of `relint E_l intersect Z^n` are disjoint for different `l`, in the affine lattice of `B`.
* Consequently `h<=2^k`.

For the parity assertion, fix an integer point `z_0 in B` and the rank-`k` lattice

    Lambda_B = lin(B-B) intersect Z^n.

Its rank is `k` because `B` is generated by integer points. Its affine coset contains every integer point in `aff B`. If `p in relint E_l` and `q in relint E_m` have the same class modulo `2 Lambda_B`, their midpoint is an integer point of `B`. A face containing that midpoint must contain both endpoints: apply any supporting affine functional and use the equality of its minimum at their average. Its minimal face consequently contains both `E_l` and `E_m`. This is another member of the family `E(z)`, contradicting maximality when the two maximal faces are distinct. There are exactly `2^k` classes in `Lambda_B/2 Lambda_B`, proving the bound.

This asserts disjoint parity sets only for the RELATIVE INTERIORS of these maximal faces. Their boundaries may overlap, and their full sets of sampled bases may share parities. No lower bound `2^(dim E_l)` on the number of relative-interior parities is asserted.

## 5. Each face piece has continuous affine rank at most d-2

For each maximal sampled face define

    F_l = F intersect projection_z^{-1}(E_l).

It is an exposed face of `F`: choose an affine base functional `B_l(z)>=0` on `B`, with zero set there exactly `E_l`. Then `F_l=F intersect {B_l(z)=0}`. Its projection is precisely `E_l`.

Choose an integer `z_l in relint E_l`. Formula (3) and (2) give

    dim F_l-dim E_l = dim (F_l)_(z_l) = dim F_(z_l) <= d-2.     (5)

Thus each piece has vertical affine kernel, or continuous affine rank, at most `d-2`. Their union contains EVERY sampled point of `F`, since the maximal sampled base faces cover `B intersect Z^n`.

If `F` is a zero facet, all these `E_l` are proper faces of `B`, since its relative interior is lattice-free. In that case both the base dimension and the continuous affine rank drop on every piece. More generally, if `B` has a relative-interior integer point, its only maximal sampled face is `B` itself, and (5) says that the whole zero face already has continuous rank at most `d-2`.

## 6. Exact restriction of the rate payment to these pieces

The moving-hinge theorem localizes the directional payment first to `F={A=0}`. Once restricted to `F`, use the convex tests

    (f-j B_l(z))_+,

which decrease on `F` to `f 1_(F_l)`. Although `B_l` need not be nonnegative elsewhere on `C`, this second limit is performed only after the first restriction. Equivalently one may use the globally convex fields `[f-i A-j B_l]_+`, first let `i` increase at fixed `j`, and then let `j` increase. The first limit is dominated on `C` by a finite bound depending on that fixed `j`; the second is dominated by `f` on `F`. Therefore both successive limits are legitimate.

For every `l`, every positive rate `R`, and every admissible nonnegative convex physical `f`, the exact right-limit payment becomes

    int_(F_l) f d v_e^noninside(R)
      +R int_(F_l) f d v_e(R)
      +int_R^infinity int_(F_l) f d v_e(s) ds
       <= beta int_(F_l) f d v_e(R),                            (6)

with the analogous left-limit version. The full cap law and the exact `beta` are unchanged. No factor `2^k` is paid in any individual restriction. If a zero-face defect is nonzero, at least one of these finitely many pieces carries nonzero defect mass.

The pieces may overlap. Summing (6) would count their intersections with multiplicity, so no mass partition or numerical summation rule is inferred. More importantly, the restricted defect measures in (6) can be singular and are not proved to equal Hausdorff volume on `F_l`. The geometric continuous-rank drop is real; converting it into an inductive OC payment requires an additional measure statement.
